newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BROKER REAFFIRMS "HOLD+" RATING ON BEKAERT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BROKER REAFFIRMS "HOLD+" RATING ON BEKAERT.

text.p: Belgian brokerage KB-Securities said on Wednesday it was still recommending investors accumulate shares in steel cord and wire maker Bekaert which have suffered heavy losses this week after a company profit warning.

Pascale Weber, analyst at KB Securities, said she reconfirmed her "accumulate" or "hold-plus" recommendation on Bekaert, based on a current price level of 18,475 francs which implied a P/E of 16.7 for 1997 and 14.0 for 1998.
Bekaert shares closed 8.4 percent or 1,675 francs down at 18,150 on Wednesday, after peaking at 20,000 at the start of the day.
"The restructuring efforts will lead to lower costs (depreciation and labour). Furthermore, Bekaert's expansion potential in fast growing markets remains intact," said Weber.
She said that Bekaert management recognised production capacity in Western Europe would need to be reduced as competition from low cost producers intensified.

"It is regrettable that a blue chip Belgian company like Bekaert is forced to reduce its production capacity in its home country because of high costs. This illustrates the fragility of Belgium's competitiveness," she added.
